question: In a vernier caliper, a retainer is used to:

options.text: block a movable part to allow the easy transferring of a measurement
measure the internal diameter of an object

solution:
The correct answer is **to block a movable part to allow the easy transferring of a measurement.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vernier Caliper**

 
 
• In **1631,** a French mathematician named** Pierre Vernier** created the vernier scale.
 
• The term "vernier caliper" refers to a measuring instrument that is used to measure** linear dimensions.**
 
• With the help of the measuring jaws, it is also used to measure the **diameters of round objects.**
 
• When compared to the **main scale**, the vernier caliper's primary function is to take **precise measurements.**
 
• The** vernier constant **is another name for the least number of vernier calipers. The difference between one **main scale division **and** one vernier scale division** is what it is defined as.
 
• The vernier caliper has a **minimum count of 0.1 mm.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Applications of Vernier Caliper**

 
 
• Medical usages
 
• Science labs
 
• Industries such as steel and aerospace
 
• Educational sectors
